title: Broadcast uses --skip-simulation with an offline-derived stale-able minBPT; no live re-query enforced
variantNote: :broadcast-specific. The documented broadcast command (script header line 55) runs with --skip-simulation --slow, so forge does not pre-execute the final pool(minBPT) against live state; the stale-floor failure modes only manifest on the actual broadcast path, not in dry/preview.
description: The final step of the cutover, _step15_pool (lines 542-602), seeds the new pool and calls pool(minBPT) where minBPT is a slippage FLOOR. minBPT defaults to DEFAULT_MIN_BPT = 284e18 (line 108), derived OFFLINE from a one-time Balancer Router ideal-BPT quote against a snapshot of seed/pool state (overridable via MIN_BPT_WEI env, line 566). The documented broadcast command (script header, line 55) uses --skip-simulation --slow, so forge does not pre-execute pool(minBPT) against current live state and cannot catch a stale floor. The script reads the seed live (partially self-correcting) but does not re-query the minBPT floor live at broadcast time, and there is no on-chain guard forcing a live re-derivation. The code comment itself instructs the operator to 'Re-query before broadcast if state moved' (lines 106-107), making the safety dependent on an out-of-band operator step.
impact: No direct asset theft. Two bounded, operator-conditioned tail risks: (a) a too-HIGH stale minBPT reverts the final pool() AFTER the irreversible broadcast steps 3-14 have already applied (dispatcher re-pointed, funds swept), stranding a half-applied cutover that needs manual owner repair — an availability concern, not a standing protocol break; (b) a too-LOW stale minBPT weakens slippage protection on the single LP add, exposing it to sandwich/slippage value leak. Both require material pool/seed drift beyond the held margin between offline derivation and broadcast, and the operator skipping the documented live re-query.
attackPath: 1. minBPT is derived offline (DEFAULT_MIN_BPT=284e18, line 108) for a snapshot seed/pool state and is not re-queried live at broadcast.
2. Pool composition or seed size drifts materially between derivation and broadcast.
3. Broadcast runs with --skip-simulation (line 55), so forge does not catch the stale floor; pool() either reverts (too-high, after steps 3-14 already applied) or under-protects the LP add (too-low).

evidence.offlineConstant: DEFAULT_MIN_BPT = 284e18 (line 108), comment notes it was derived from a live offline router query and instructs 'Re-query before broadcast if state moved' (lines 106-107).
evidence.envOverride: minBPT = vm.envOr("MIN_BPT_WEI", DEFAULT_MIN_BPT) (line 566) — no live on-chain re-derivation enforced.
evidence.skipSimulation: Documented broadcast command uses --rpc-url $RPC_MAINNET --broadcast --skip-simulation --slow (script header, line 55).
evidence.marginAtAudit: At the audit block a ~1.4% margin held (seed 527.80 sUSDS, 287.9 BPT minted vs 284e18 floor); seed is read live so the path is partially self-correcting.

recommendation: Either re-derive minBPT live inside _step15_pool via the Balancer Router queryAddLiquidityUnbalanced against the actual current seed (and apply the slippage bps to the live quote) rather than trusting an offline constant, or refuse to broadcast when MIN_BPT_WEI is not explicitly supplied for the current state. If --skip-simulation must be kept (for --slow nonce sequencing), add an in-script live freshness assert on the quote so a drifted floor aborts BEFORE the irreversible steps rather than at the final pool().

poc.note: Low severity; no coded PoC required. Failure modes are operator-conditioned and were not reproduced under realistic drift at the audit block (margin held).

classification.reasoning: C4 Low/QA: script-design / stale-offline-parameter observation. No demonstrated value leak under realistic conditions (margin held), failure modes operator-conditioned and recoverable, self-correcting live seed read plus documented re-query keep realistic likelihood low. Does not meet Medium (no standing function/availability break or value leak under stated assumptions).
